definition: A rectangular array of numbers in rows and columns: a matrix with $m$ rows and $n$ columns has order $m \times n$ (rows first), and $a_{ij}$ is the element in row $i$, column $j$.

Forming the product $AB$, which exists only when $A$ has as many columns as $B$ has rows; each element of $AB$ is a row of $A$ times a column of $B$ (multiply matching pairs, then add), and in general $AB \neq BA$.
The square matrix $I$ with $1$s on the leading diagonal and $0$s everywhere else, so that $AI = IA = A$ for any square matrix $A$ of the same order.
A number, written $\det A$ or $|A|$, worked out from a square matrix $A$: for a $2 \times 2$ matrix with rows $a, b$ and $c, d$ it is $ad - bc$, and $A$ has an inverse only when $\det A \neq 0$.

For a square matrix $A$ with $\det A \neq 0$, the matrix $A^{-1}$ with $AA^{-1} = A^{-1}A = I$; a matrix with $\det A = 0$ has no inverse, and $A\boldsymbol{x} = \boldsymbol{b}$ gives $\boldsymbol{x} = A^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$, multiplying on the left.
